vss.text:
VSS READER
State	ready
Messages read	11
Its drawing	12 shapes · 4 links · 7 steps to undo
Requests cut by	VSS cutter (its own cutter: the cut its confidence was fitted on)
Ready: 9 micro-worlds, 31.4 MB, loaded in 0.3 s.

Nine small VSS readers (micro-worlds), each trained on a few actions of SOP Lang (VSA route books, no transformer). The world cutter names the worlds that could read each request (it also cuts the message: the VSS cutter, this tab’s own cut); each of those worlds reads it, and the reading that leaves the fewest words not understood is kept (no drawing is passed to a world). A tie, and a reference such as “it” or a role left empty, go to the context filler, which fills it from the conversation and the names on the canvas when one candidate ranks first, and asks otherwise (the rule of 2026-11-01). In a world with several actions, a request without a verb (“Hub teal”) gets its action from a second cutter (the event hint). The files come from this site and load when the page opens.

How the VSS reader works What a VSS world is

WHEN VSS ACTS

VSS executes a request only when its confidence clears the threshold of the level chosen here (by default its safety threshold: the one that scores best when a confident mistake costs as much as 10 right answers; “boldest”, “very bold”, “bolder” and “more careful” are the same rule with a mistake counted as 1, 2, 5 or 20 right answers, see the table below); below it, it does not execute the request, says why it is not sure and offers Do it anyway. The confidence combines 13 numbers from VSS’s own chain (the cut, the world, the reading, the words, the context filler) with whether SOP-BERT and the Rules, reading the same request (VSS’s own cut: they read the VSS cutter’s requests for this), read it the same way (and whether the Rules had a note about it). Commands and questions have their own threshold. It was fitted on the calibration part of the fresh2 and short3 messages, from out-of-fold scores (the refit of 2026-11-03 for the 9 worlds: votes as inputs, no world prior, a threshold for commands and one for questions), and on the test part it did better than VSS’s confidence without the votes: cost score 22.9 against 4.8, difference +18.2 (95% interval 11.9 to 24.7), 37.8% of the requests done right instead of 5.3%. So a held request’s reason first says who reads it differently (“SOP-BERT reads colour ‘red’ instead of colour ‘blue’”), then what VSS itself was unsure of. When SOP-BERT has not read the message (still loading, or not available), VSS uses its confidence without the votes (confidence/vss.json, version 09386a14df) at the same level, and the details say so.

neural.text:
SOP-BERT READER
State	ready
Messages read	11
Its drawing	12 shapes · 4 links · 6 steps to undo
Requests cut by	BERT cutter (its own cutter: the cut its confidence was fitted on)

SOP-BERT: one DistilBERT model of ours, fine-tuned on the same annotated requests as the VSS worlds, run in this browser. In two calls per message (the cut, then all its requests at once) it reads, for every request, the action, the value of each SOP Lang key, who fills each role (a name written in the request, “it”, or a description such as “the red circle”) and the words that are names, labels and numbers; the SOP Lang wires are then assembled by the legend. It does not use the Rules reader. It carries out a request only when its confidence clears the threshold chosen below, and asks about the rest. Its cut head is the BERT cutter: the cut this tab and VSS-BERT read. The files come from this site, load by themselves when the page opens, and stay in this browser’s cache.

How SOP-BERT works What we do with BERT

Model
SOP-BERT · 68.7 MB
DistilBERT fine-tuned on our requests — cuts the message, reads the action, the values, the names and the descriptions (base model distilbert-base-uncased). README · version fd69a08c3b
Device
CPU (WASM), 8-bit files

Ready: SOP-BERT on the CPU (WASM, 8-bit files), 68.7 MB, loaded in 1.9 s from the browser cache.

WHEN SOP-BERT ACTS

SOP-BERT executes a request only when its confidence clears the threshold of the level chosen here (by default its safety threshold, the one that scores best when a confident mistake costs as much as 10 right answers; “boldest”, “very bold”, “bolder” and “more careful” count a mistake as 1, 2, 5 or 20 right answers, see the table below); below it, it does not execute the request, says why it is not sure and offers Do it anyway. The confidence combines 24 numbers read from the model’s own outputs for that request (the action, the values, who fills each role, the word tags, the cut, the word pieces, how often its action is read right) with whether VSS and the Rules, reading the same request (they read the BERT cutter’s requests for this), read it the same way (and whether the Rules had a note about it). Commands and questions have their own threshold. It was fitted on requests of the BERT cutter, on the calibration part of the fresh2 and short3 messages, from out-of-fold scores (the refit of 2026-11-03 for the new SOP-BERT: votes as inputs, a threshold for commands and one for questions); on the test part it scored 33.4 against 29.3 for SOP-BERT’s confidence without the votes, difference +4.0 (95% interval −2.4 to 9.8: not shown either way), confidently wrong on 2.5% of what it executed instead of 3.0%. A held request’s reason first says who reads it differently, then what SOP-BERT itself was unsure of. When VSS has not read the message (still loading, or not available), SOP-BERT uses its confidence without the votes (confidence/sop-bert.json, version 769d3f4293) at the same level.

combined.text:
VSS-BERT READER
State	ready
Messages read	11
Its drawing	11 shapes · 3 links · 2 steps to undo
Requests cut by	BERT cutter (its own cutter: the cut its confidence was fitted on)

VSS-BERT is not a third model: it is VSS and SOP-BERT reading the same requests, and it does what they are sure of together. Both read the requests of the BERT cutter (SOP-BERT’s cut head: the cut with which this combination scored best, and the one its confidence was fitted on). Nothing is read again for VSS-BERT: SOP-BERT’s reading is the SOP-BERT tab’s, and VSS’s reading of the same requests is the one made for SOP-BERT’s votes. The two readings of each request are paired: when both readers have it, SOP-BERT’s reading is the one executed; when only one has it, that one. Each request gets a combined confidence: the executing reader’s own numbers, whether the two readers agree (all the values, or a share of them) and VSS’s own confidence. When the two agree, a request is right about 95% of the time, so agreement raises the confidence; when they disagree, or only one reader found the request, it is lowered. Below the threshold it asks, says why, and offers Do it anyway.

Two readers together
